title: Phenotype-lift source audit ledger
scope: Authoritative or individually accessible sources for normalizing raw symptoms, signs, vitals, laboratory and imaging findings; inferring higher-order physiologic phenotypes through a separate rule layer; and performing reverse differential-diagnosis retrieval.
global_finding: No audited source supplies a comprehensive, validated mapping from arbitrary sets of two or three findings plus thresholds, timing and exclusions to higher-order syndromes. Ontology subsumption, disease-phenotype association and syndrome-criteria satisfaction must remain separate relation types.

access_values.anonymous: No account or institutional purchase is required for the audited public artifact.
access_values.personal-registration: A free or territory-dependent individual account or license is required; institutional purchase is not inherently required.
access_values.click-through: No personal account was required in the audited path, but the user must accept source-specific terms before download or use.

recommendation_tiers.P0_core: Recommended for the first reproducible implementation, subject to the stated redistribution guard.
recommendation_tiers.P1_optional_enhancement: Useful enhancement that must not block the anonymous/open MVP.
recommendation_tiers.P2_manual_or_weak_reference: Use for manual rule seeding, implementation examples or weak candidate generation, not as automatic truth.
recommendation_tiers.excluded_as_semantic_inference_source: May validate identifiers or labels, but is not suitable for ontology or syndrome inference.

sources.name: Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO)
sources.license: HPO custom license terms; free access with attribution/citation, public display of date/version, and restrictions against altering distributed content or logical relationships.
best_role: Normalize symptoms, signs and abnormal laboratory phenotypes to stable HPO identifiers
Use labels, synonyms, definitions, obsolete replacements and true is-a ancestors for lexical retrieval and safe abstraction
not_sufficient_for: Inferring a syndrome from co-occurring sibling findings
Encoding has-phenotype or diagnostic-criteria relations as subclass relations
Comprehensive coverage of common acute syndromes
sources.redistribution_guard: Preserve source labels and logical relationships, include the HPO license/citation and exact release date, and keep local aliases or inferred rules in a separate namespace rather than modifying HPO content.

sources.name: HPO disease annotations (phenotype.hpoa / HPOA)
sources.version_or_snapshot: HPO v2026-06-23 release annotation assets
sources.license: HPO custom license terms plus source-specific rights for underlying disease annotations; OMIM-derived IEA annotations have an explicit additional reuse warning.
best_role: Reverse retrieval from normalized HPO findings to rare or hereditary diseases
Weight disease candidates using frequency, onset, sex, modifiers, evidence and explicit negative annotations
not_sufficient_for: Defining a higher-order phenotype from its component findings
Broad common-disease or acute-care syndrome coverage
Unfiltered redistribution of all annotation rows
sources.redistribution_guard: Filter and retain row-level provenance. HPO documentation states that OMIM-parsed IEA annotations require contacting OMIM before reuse in other software products; prefer ORPHA, PMID-backed PCS/TAS or other reuse-safe provenance for published derivatives.

sources.name: LOINC2HPO annotation data and software
sources.version_or_snapshot: Annotation repository HEAD c1068d6d6b80ce757ff7a26e4c38a5ac8e7c830c (2021-11-07); audited TSV: 7,415 rows, 3,118 unique LOINC codes and 827 unique HPO terms
sources.license: Annotation repository permission grant with required notices; incorporated LOINC-derived content remains subject to the LOINC license. The Java software is BSD-3-Clause.
best_role: High-precision single-observation mapping from LOINC plus H/L/N, POS/NEG or selected nominal result values to HPO
Normalize already interpreted laboratory abnormalities such as low potassium to Hypokalemia
not_sufficient_for: Mapping uncoded free text directly
Computing laboratory reference ranges or abnormality direction
Combining multiple observations into a syndrome
Current comprehensive LOINC coverage
sources.redistribution_guard: Pin the exact commit, carry the annotation license and LOINC notice, label the data as a stale 2021 snapshot, and do not represent its academic mappings as clinical diagnostic advice.

sources.name: RadLex
sources.version_or_snapshot: v4.3; official portal snapshot listed 34,446 active classes, 455 retired classes and 58,065 total terms
sources.license: RadLex License Agreement and Terms of Use Version 2.1, last updated 2025-01-06; worldwide no-charge and royalty-free grant subject to attribution, notice and adaptation restrictions.
best_role: Normalize radiology findings, anatomy and imaging-specific expressions
Provide exact imaging identifiers, source labels, synonyms and ontology relations
not_sufficient_for: General symptom normalization outside radiology
Inferring physiologic syndromes from imaging findings
Definition-based embeddings for all terms because most classes lack definitions
sources.redistribution_guard: Include the license and all source notices. Do not modify clinical-term RID, names or translations, synonyms, or original ontologic relations; keep any added aliases and rules in a clearly marked adaptation layer.

sources.name: Mondo Disease Ontology
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
best_role: Normalize disease, syndrome and higher-order target labels
Resolve cross-database disease identifiers and synonyms
not_sufficient_for: Mapping component findings to syndrome criteria
Treating prose disease definitions as executable rules without curation
sources.redistribution_guard: Retain attribution and exact release provenance; distinguish Mondo equivalence axioms and xrefs from locally asserted clinical rules.

sources.name: Human Disease Ontology (DO)
sources.version_or_snapshot: Current production PURL audited 2026-08-25; July 2026 production OBO/JSON representation transition active
best_role: Supplement Mondo with common disease and syndrome target labels, definitions, synonyms and hierarchy
Provide a permissively redistributable target terminology
not_sufficient_for: Automatic extraction of multi-finding syndrome rules from free-text definitions
Observation-level normalization
sources.redistribution_guard: Pin the exact downloaded commit or release and test the parser because the July 2026 production-format change may break older OBO/OBGraphs JSON readers.

sources.name: Orphadata phenotypes associated with rare disorders
sources.version_or_snapshot: Orphanet knowledge-base release July 2026; English en_product4.xml dated 2026-06-23 with 4,357 disorders
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
best_role: Redistributable HPO-to-rare-disease association layer
Reverse differential-diagnosis retrieval with Orphanet disorder identifiers
not_sufficient_for: Common acute syndrome coverage
Defining syndrome composition from raw findings
sources.redistribution_guard: Retain Orphadata attribution, release date, language and source identifiers; do not merge frequency or absence semantics into an untyped binary edge.

sources.name: Monarch Knowledge Graph
sources.version_or_snapshot: Monarch KG release shown as 2026-07-14 on the official portal; source integration is updated approximately monthly
sources.license: Open-access integrated resource with edge-level source provenance; underlying source licenses remain applicable.
best_role: Download the disease-to-phenotypic-feature association product for reverse differential diagnosis
Integrate HPO, Mondo, Orphanet and other source identifiers using Biolink/KGX
not_sufficient_for: Defining a syndrome from a component-finding set
Treating every integrated edge as equally licensed or clinically authoritative
Complete common-disease coverage
sources.redistribution_guard: Preserve primary knowledge-source provenance and license metadata. Prefer the narrow association download over the full KG and source-filter any published derivative.

sources.name: NCBI MedGen
sources.version_or_snapshot: Weekly FTP/API data, audited 2026-08-25; documentation last updated April 2026
sources.license: US-government-created material is public domain with requested attribution; contributed or licensed source vocabulary material remains subject to the original rights holder's terms.
best_role: Source-filtered clinical synonym and identifier crosswalk
Use MGCONSO, MGREL, MGSTY, MedGenIDMappings and MedGen_HPO_Mapping for lexical rescue and reverse disease links
Programmatic search of multiple clinical features with Entrez esearch/esummary
not_sufficient_for: Unfiltered public redistribution of all source atoms
Using manifestation associations as syndrome definitions
Assuming all strings assigned to one UMLS CUI are task-equivalent
sources.redistribution_guard: Filter every published derivative by SAB/source and semantic type. Exclude or separately license OMIM, SNOMED CT and other restricted atoms; retain MedGen attribution and source identifiers.

sources.name: OHDSI Phenotype Library
sources.version_or_snapshot: R package v3.37.0 dated 2026-04-08; official 2025-04-02 usage vignette showed 703 cohort definitions
sources.license: Apache License 2.0 for the repository and package; terminology concepts referenced by definitions may retain their own source licenses.
best_role: Study versioned computable cohort logic, inclusion and exclusion clauses, time windows and code-list handling
Manually select a small number of measurement-rich definitions as rule-engineering exemplars
not_sufficient_for: Direct short-vignette syndrome composition
A broad atomic-finding lexicon
Automatic reuse of all OMOP vocabulary content without source-license review
sources.redistribution_guard: Keep cohort-definition version/DOI and review the license of every referenced OMOP source vocabulary before redistributing resolved code lists.

sources.name: PheKB public phenotype catalog
sources.version_or_snapshot: Public catalog snapshot audited 2026-08-25
sources.license: No clear catalog-wide machine-redistribution license was identified on the audited official public catalog; individual artifacts and contributed files may have separate rights.
best_role: Manual review of EHR phenotype algorithms using diagnoses, laboratories, medications, vitals and NLP
Validation or design reference for a small set of named phenotypes
not_sufficient_for: A general symptom-to-syndrome knowledge base
Reliable repository-wide bulk download
Unreviewed bulk redistribution
sources.redistribution_guard: Review artifact-specific ownership and terms before copying files. Do not scrape and commit the public catalog as though it had one open-data license.

sources.name: PheMA PheKB phenotypes in CQL and FHIR
sources.version_or_snapshot: Moving GitHub main snapshot audited 2026-08-25; repository lists 33 translated phenotypes
sources.license: No clear repository-wide LICENSE file or explicit bulk-content license was identified in the audited official repository.
best_role: Study concrete CQL, FHIR ValueSet and synthetic-test implementations of selected PheKB algorithms
Reuse the testing pattern after independently authoring licensed local rules
not_sufficient_for: Comprehensive phenotype coverage
Automatic clinical truth
Safe bulk redistribution until licensing is clarified
sources.redistribution_guard: Pin the studied commit and treat repository content as reference-only until the maintainers clarify the license; do not copy its phenotype definitions into a published data product by default.

sources.name: DisMech Disorder Mechanisms Knowledge Base
sources.version_or_snapshot: Active pre-alpha moving main snapshot audited 2026-08-25; portal listed 1,298 disorders, 2,051 subtypes, 21,000+ cited publications and 1,796 research reports
sources.license: Content CC BY 4.0; repository software BSD-3-Clause.
best_role: Generate weak candidates for mechanistic bridge rules and explanations
Locate PubMed-backed pathophysiology and phenotype evidence for subsequent independent validation
not_sufficient_for: Hard rule activation, candidate deletion or veto
Clinical diagnosis or individual laboratory interpretation
Stable released identifiers or even coverage
sources.redistribution_guard: Pin an exact git commit. Preserve evidence citations and label all derived rules as unvalidated candidates; official documentation states that most content is AI-authored, human review is not line-by-line re-derivation, and scientific errors are expected.

sources.name: LOINC
sources.version_or_snapshot: v2.83 released 2026-08-19; official FHIR terminology service still documented v2.81 on the audit date
sources.license: LOINC license; free for commercial and non-commercial use, with attribution, integrity and anti-competing-standard conditions.
best_role: Identify the observation, measurement, specimen, method, component and property
Disambiguate tests before applying result-interpretation logic
not_sufficient_for: Determining whether an observed result is high or low
Mapping raw prose to a clinical syndrome
Encoding multi-finding criteria
sources.redistribution_guard: Carry the current LOINC license and attribution, do not modify or use the content to promulgate a competing observation standard, and do not assume third-party survey content has identical rights.

sources.name: Unified Medical Language System (UMLS)
sources.version_or_snapshot: 2026AA released 2026-05-04; full release 5.3 GB compressed and 40.1 GB uncompressed
sources.license: Free individual UMLS Metathesaurus license and UTS account; source vocabularies may impose additional agreements, restrictions or fees; annual-use reporting normally applies.
best_role: Lexical normalization, source-aware synonym lookup and terminology crosswalk
Use MRCONSO, semantic types and carefully source-filtered MRREL relationships for candidate retrieval
not_sufficient_for: Conjunctive syndrome rules
Treating all atoms in a CUI as interchangeable
Unfiltered public redistribution
sources.redistribution_guard: Filter by source abbreviation and source restriction level, retain every source license, and never commit or redistribute the full UMLS release as an open project artifact.

sources.name: SNOMED CT International Edition
sources.version_or_snapshot: August 2026 International Edition released 2026-08-01
sources.license: SNOMED CT Affiliate/National license. Use is normally free in member countries after registration; fees and reporting may apply in non-member territories.
best_role: Rich clinical finding and disorder terminology with descriptions, is-a hierarchy, logical definitions and attributes
Optional high-coverage normalizer and ontology substrate in licensed deployments
not_sufficient_for: A generally redistributable anonymous project dependency
Automatically validated syndrome criteria including thresholds and timing
Inferring co-occurrence as a logical definition
sources.redistribution_guard: Do not commit full RF2 or derived semantic subsets to a public repository without confirming Affiliate, national, territorial and downstream sublicense obligations. Pin the exact release package.

sources.name: SNOMED CT Global Patient Set (GPS)
sources.version_or_snapshot: 2026 production package announced 2026-03-11; freeset file SnomedINTL_GPSRelease_PRODUCTION_20260101T120000Z.txt
sources.license: Official sources conflict: the March 2026 announcement states CC BY-ND 4.0, while the current technical guide states CC BY 4.0. The stricter CC BY-ND 4.0 interpretation is required pending clarification.
best_role: Validate and display SNOMED CT identifiers, FSNs, US preferred terms and active/inactive status in unlicensed environments
not_sufficient_for: Hierarchy traversal, parent or ancestor queries, subsumption or ECL
Logical definitions, relationship-based analytics or decision support
Syndrome or phenotype inference
sources.redistribution_guard: Treat identifiers as flat opaque codes, record the GPS release, avoid derivative semantic products, and apply CC BY-ND until SNOMED International resolves the official license discrepancy.

sources.name: Clinical Quality Language (CQL) specification and tooling
sources.version_or_snapshot: CQL tooling release 4.8.0 dated 2026-05-08
sources.license: Apache License 2.0 for code and tooling; CC BY 4.0 for documentation.
best_role: Represent and validate typed clinical rules with Boolean logic, thresholds, time windows, terminology bindings and exclusions
Compile human-readable rules to ELM and execute them deterministically
not_sufficient_for: Providing the medical criteria or evidence used by a rule
Lexically normalizing nonstandard vignette text
Serving as a syndrome knowledge base by itself
sources.redistribution_guard: Keep medical rule content, its evidence license and terminology licenses separate from the Apache-licensed execution tooling; version every local rule independently.

sources.name: WHO SMART Guidelines and Digital Adaptation Kits
sources.version_or_snapshot: Moving WHO SMART catalog and artifact-specific implementation guides audited 2026-08-25
sources.license: Artifact-specific WHO terms, frequently a Creative Commons IGO license; maturity and implementation permissions differ by guide and draft status.
best_role: Authoritative domain-specific seeds for data dictionaries, decision-support logic, workflows and FHIR/CQL implementation patterns
Model provenance-rich rule packages rather than an untyped syndrome dictionary
not_sufficient_for: Broad cross-specialty syndrome coverage
Assuming every SMART draft is implementation-ready
Applying one catalog-wide redistribution license
sources.redistribution_guard: Check the exact guide version, status and license before extraction; do not implement draft artifacts that prohibit implementation, and preserve WHO attribution plus rule-level source provenance.

sources.name: DiagRL-Corpus Guideline_common and Guideline_rare snapshot
sources.version_or_snapshot: QiaoyuZheng/DiagRL-Corpus commit 402ff97d2eb076da2da7086eed7aa2c4c897b9ea; local files are byte-identical
sources.license: Hugging Face dataset card declares Apache-2.0, while individual common-disease rows attribute heterogeneous third-party web sources and rare rows are described as Orphanet-derived.
best_role: Existing exploratory disease-label and symptom-profile corpus for local retrieval smoke tests
Diagnose whether a proposed phenotype query can address a target label already present in the frozen corpus
not_sufficient_for: An openly redistributable medical knowledge base without transitive-source review
Clinical truth, syndrome definitions or confirmatory retrieval evaluation
Measuring end-to-end binder performance when queries are manually curated
sources.redistribution_guard: Retain the pinned dataset commit and row-level source URLs. Do not assume the dataset-level Apache tag resolves copyright or terms for Mayo, WebMD, Merck or other underlying excerpts; replace or filter rows before an open production release.

sources.name: Repository clinical-practice-guideline (CPG) chunk corpus
sources.version_or_snapshot: cursor4 a945aa57; 205,115 chunks from 8,038 unique articles
sources.license: Mixed per-chunk provenance: PMC CC BY/CC0/CC BY-NC/CC BY-ND/CC BY-NC-ND/NO-CC and author manuscripts, WikEM CC BY-SA, 3,311 purchased Merck Manual 19e chunks, plus guideline chunks with missing local license notes.
best_role: Repository-local sparse and MedCPT retrieval smoke tests with per-chunk provenance
Build a separately filtered open-license research tranche
not_sufficient_for: A homogeneous open corpus
Redistribution or deployment without per-source license filtering
Clinical entailment or blinded document relevance labels
sources.redistribution_guard: Use license_note as a hard gate. The conservative open replay retains only PMC CC BY, PMC CC0 and WikEM CC BY-SA; exclude purchased, NC, ND, NO-CC and missing-license chunks unless separately authorized. Add article-level deduplication and section-quality filtering.

sources.name: MedCPT Query and Article Encoders
sources.version_or_snapshot: Query Encoder commit d83a36cc6b8e3a5c5e9d9d6ba156808c1643dcbc; query model.safetensors SHA-256 19d78c0d5eaee2f81e6c47c5425bbadcc0c6af016cbb5da4a000d64e59d6e342
sources.license: Model card and bundled LICENSE identify the NCBI model as public domain; the model card includes a research/clinical-oversight disclaimer.
best_role: Dense proposal retrieval for non-literal biomedical queries
Rank fusion with lexical retrieval after corpus-license and section-quality filters
not_sufficient_for: Determining thresholds, assertion, subject, time or specimen
Inferring that a syndrome or relation is clinically true
Overriding source-corpus licenses
sources.redistribution_guard: Pin encoder commit and weight hash, preserve the public-domain LICENSE and model disclaimer, and treat every retrieved document under its own source license. Do not use similarity as a clinical evidence edge.
